questions.knowledge_point: Calculating a Vector Projection Using Components
questions.problem: Let $a=⟨2,-2,9⟩$ and $b=⟨1,-1,1⟩.$ Find the vector projection of $a$ onto $b.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,a & =\frac{a\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{b}_{x}^{2}+{b}_{y}^{2}+{b}_{z}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 1+(-2)\cdot (-1)+9\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{13}{3}⟨1,-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{13}{3},-\frac{13}{3},\frac{13}{3}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $a=[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ 3\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]$ and $b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$ Find the vector projection of $b$ onto $a.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,b & =\frac{a\cdot b}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{{a}_{x}{b}_{x}+{a}_{y}{b}_{y}+{a}_{z}{b}_{z}}{{a}_{x}^{2}+{a}_{y}^{2}+{a}_{z}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{6\cdot 3+3\cdot 1+3\sqrt{2}\cdot 0}{{6}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(3\sqrt{2})^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{21}{63}⟨6,3,3\sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{3}⟨6,3,3\sqrt{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨2,1,\sqrt{2}⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.worked_solution:
Since $u$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $v$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular. 

So, we must have

$$
u⊥v\,⟹\,u\cdot v=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & ={u}_{x}\cdot {v}_{x}+{u}_{y}\cdot {v}_{y}+{u}_{z}\cdot {v}_{z} \\  & =4\cdot k+2\cdot (-1)+(-3)\cdot 5 \\  & =4k-2-15 \\  & =4k-17.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}u\cdot v & =0 \\ 4k-17 & =0 \\ 4k & =17 \\ k & =\frac{17}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Let $r=\,i+3j+4k$ and $s=3i-j.$ Find the vector projection of $r$ onto $s.$

${\text{proj}}_{s}\,r=⟨$
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}$,$
{{field-3}}
$⟩$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula for the vector projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{s}\,r & =\frac{r\cdot s}{s\cdot s}s \\  & =\frac{{r}_{x}{s}_{x}+{r}_{y}{s}_{y}+{r}_{z}{s}_{z}}{{s}_{x}^{2}+{s}_{y}^{2}+{s}_{z}^{2}}s \\  & =\frac{(1)\cdot 3+(3)\cdot (-1)+(4)\cdot 0}{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}s \\  & =\frac{0}{{3}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}s \\  & =⟨0,0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $a$ is a nonzero vector, its projection onto another nonzero vector $b$ equals the zero vector only when the vectors are perpendicular.

So, we must have

$$
a⊥b\,⟹\,a\cdot b=0.
$$

Computing the dot product, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & ={a}_{x}\cdot {b}_{x}+{a}_{y}\cdot {b}_{y}+{a}_{z}\cdot {b}_{z} \\  & =t\cdot 4+(-4)\cdot 1+1\cdot 0 \\  & =4t-4+0 \\  & =4t-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Setting the dot product equal to $0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot b & =0 \\ 4t-4 & =0 \\ 4t & =4 \\ t & =1 \\ t & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
